tasks.short: Collect scores from session sheets, enter them, make charts per goal, write a short explanation, check the charts, and send them to the speech-language pathologist.

steps.what: Speech therapy assistant collects clients' scores from paper session sheets
Speech therapy assistant enters scores in a spreadsheet
Speech therapy assistant prepares charts and graphs of clients' performance per goal
Speech therapy assistant writes a short explanation of the charts
Speech therapy assistant checks the final charts and explanation
Speech therapy assistant shares the checked charts with the speech-language pathologist: by e-mail today, by saving them in the therapy record after the change

tasks.design: Scores are entered during the session on a tablet in score fields per goal in the therapy record ({OTHER}), so they are not collected from paper sheets and typed into a spreadsheet; sessions held on paper, about 20%, are still typed in. The record charts progress per goal from the scores by fixed rules, and the assistant picks which charts to show and writes the explanation. Once checked, the assistant saves the charts in the record for the speech-language pathologist instead of e-mailing them; this is an ordinary save that needs no approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scores were written on paper, typed into spreadsheets and charted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Therapy records take scores per goal and chart them.
tasks.still_hard: School visits often happen without a tablet.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the chart that shows a parent real progress.
tasks.altitude: The assistant explains progress instead of building charts.

evidence.claim: Therapy records can take scores per goal and chart progress over time.
Health data are special category; care use rests on article 9(2)(h) with professional secrecy.

assumptions: Boundary: from sessions held to charts sent; treatment decisions are outside.
Input contract: score fields set per goal by the pathologist; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.
Scenario: about 80% of sessions are scored on a tablet; the rest on paper.
The assistant checks every chart before it is shared; s6 keeps 20 for saving them in the record.

incremental.description: Speech therapy assistant fixes score entries made under the wrong goal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half the sessions stay on paper, so s1 keeps 60 and s2 keeps 50 (48.0); high: about 80% of sessions scored on a tablet (61.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Test equipment, clean and maintain it, write results in the equipment log, and report faults.

steps.what: Speech therapy assistant tests equipment to ensure correct performance
Speech therapy assistant cleans and maintains equipment
Speech therapy assistant writes test results in the paper equipment log
Speech therapy assistant reports faulty equipment: by phone today; after the change completes the fault report the failed check opens
Speech therapy assistant checks the fault report: device, problem found and its urgency
Speech therapy assistant submits the checked fault report to the practice manager

tasks.design: Each device has a recurring check on a tablet checklist ({OTHER}) that stores the result per device, so tests are not written in a paper log. A failed check opens a fault report with the device and the problem; the assistant completes it, checks it and submits it once to the practice manager instead of phoning for routine faults. Testing and maintaining equipment stay with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were written in a paper log and faults reported by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Checklist apps store results per device and raise fault reports.
tasks.still_hard: Calibration by the supplier still needs arranging.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that a headset sounds slightly off.

evidence.claim: Checklist apps can store recurring check results per device and raise fault reports.
Medical devices must be maintained as the manufacturer prescribes under national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the check due to the fault reported; repairs are outside.
Input contract: devices listed in the checklist app; fallback is the paper log.

Testing does not change. s3 keeps 80 because the checklist lists the devices and the assistant still records each result; s4 keeps 50 because the report replaces a phone call; the check and the submit keep their full time.
The practice manager's time does not change.
research_questions: Are faulty devices taken out of use sooner?

incremental.description: Speech therapy assistant adds new devices to the checklist.

approvals.approved_version: The fault report with device, problem and urgency exactly as checked by the assistant in s4b, submitted once to the practice manager; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few devices and the manager still wants a call for faults, so s3 keeps 95 and s4 keeps 80 (1.8); high: many devices across locations (6.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare session materials, run in-service training or family education sessions, handle sign-ups, and record attendance.

steps.what: Speech therapy assistant prepares materials for training and education sessions
Family member or staff member signs up for a session through the online form
Speech therapy assistant handles sign-ups by e-mail and phone
Speech therapy assistant conducts in-service training sessions or family and community education programs
Speech therapy assistant records attendance on a paper list

tasks.design: Session materials are kept in a shared library per topic ({DOCS}) and adapted, instead of made each time. Families and staff sign up through an online form ({OTHER}) that shows date and place, so sign-ups are not taken by e-mail and phone, and the sign-up list is ticked off on a tablet as attendance. Running sessions stays with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were made per session and sign-ups taken by e-mail and phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Online forms take sign-ups and produce attendance lists.
tasks.still_hard: Some families need to be called to sign up.
tasks.human_edge: Showing parents how to practise speech at the dinner table.

evidence.claim: Online forms can take sign-ups and produce attendance lists.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session planned to attendance recorded; programme design by the pathologist is outside.
Input contract: form and material library set up; fallback is e-mail and paper.
Families sign up online in about the time a call took; this is priced in s3f. s4 keeps 70 because names come from the sign-up list and the assistant still marks each attendee.

incremental.description: Speech therapy assistant keeps the material library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off sessions on new topics and families who keep phoning, so s1 keeps 95 and s3 keeps 80 (6.3); high: repeated sessions with online sign-up (17.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recruit and schedule participants, collect data in sessions, enter data, transcribe speech samples, and search literature for the pathologist.

steps.what: Participant books a session through the online booking page
Speech therapy assistant recruits participants and schedules sessions by e-mail and phone
Speech therapy assistant assists the pathologist by collecting research data in sessions
Speech therapy assistant enters research data into spreadsheets
Speech therapy assistant transcribes recorded speech samples

loop.input: Recorded speech samples, made with participants' consent.
loop.output: A draft word-level transcript per sample.
loop.check: The assistant listens to every sample and corrects the transcript against the recording; samples where speech recognition marks low confidence are transcribed by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Typing every sample by hand takes several times the recording length.

steps.what: Speech therapy assistant searches literature for the pathologist

tasks.design: Participants book their sessions through an online booking page ({CALENDAR}), so the assistant schedules by e-mail and phone only for participants who cannot. Data are entered during the session into electronic data capture forms with checks ({DATA_PLATFORM}) instead of spreadsheets afterwards. Speech recognition drafts transcripts of recorded samples, and the assistant corrects every transcript against the recording. Saved literature searches send new papers. Collecting data in sessions stays with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scheduling, data entry and transcription were done by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking pages, data capture forms and speech recognition are available.
tasks.still_hard: Speech recognition works poorly on disordered speech.
tasks.human_edge: Putting a nervous child at ease before recording.
tasks.altitude: The assistant corrects transcripts instead of typing them.

evidence.claim: A census of three deployed AI scribes found verified errors in 31.3% of 565 notes.
Speech recognition can draft transcripts that a person corrects against the recording.
Health data are special category; research use needs consent or another basis under article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the study approved to sources found; analysis by the pathologist is outside.
Input contract: participants consent to recording; fallback is hand transcription.
Participants book online in about the time a call took; this is priced in s1p. s1 keeps 50 for recruiting and for participants who cannot book online.
research_questions: How long does correcting a drafted transcript take for disordered speech?

already_counted.description: Speech therapy assistant corrects drafted transcripts.

incremental.description: Speech therapy assistant sets up data capture forms per study.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: studies of severe disorders where recognition fails, so most samples are transcribed by hand and s4 keeps 85 (29.5); high: studies of mild disorders or typical speech (34.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The speech therapy assistant keeps working with clients, testing equipment, running sessions and collecting research data; typed scores, hand-made charts, paper logs and hand transcription shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An assistant with more time with clients.
